newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai bank deposits drop sharply this year.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai bank deposits drop sharply this year.

text.p: Growth of bank deposits in Shanghai fell sharply in the first five months of 1997 with last year's two cuts in bank interest rates pushing money into state debt and stocks, the Business News said on Thursday.

New deposits in Shanghai branches of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China increased by only 700 million yuan in the first five months against more than seven billion yuan last year, the newspaper said.
Sharp falls were also reported by the Shanghai branches of other major banks, the newspaper said.
"All the banks believe the two cuts in bank interest rates last year is the major reason for the fall," it said.
"Large issues of state debt this year and stock trading fever also encouraged money to flow out of the banking system."
The People's Bank of China, the central bank, cut bank interest rates in May and August last year.
The newspaper said all major banks had taken measures to improve their services to attract more bank deposits.
